successors.name: Assyria
successors.text: the rump state of Hanigalbat in the Khabur valley and the east, taken by the Middle Assyrian kings

successors.name: Hittite Empire
successors.text: the western portions, Aleppo, Mukiš and the lands west of the Euphrates

ledger.x: c. 1600 BC: the Hurrian kingdom of Mitanni appears on the Khabur. The infobox gives 'Established: c. 1600 BC'; Washukanni lies 'on the headwaters of the Khabur River'; the text dates the dynasty 'between c. 1600 and 1350 BC'. The page gives no boundary.

c. 1500 BC (bridged): Mitanni overshadows Assur. Shaushtatar (c. 1480–1460) 'sacked the Assyrian capital of Assur some time in the 15th century'; the page gives no year for the loss of the Assyrian lands, and the Assyrian dossier records Cliopatria's shrink at -1500.

c. 1500 BC: Barattarna builds the great kingdom. 'King Barattarna of Mitanni expanded the kingdom west to Aleppo' (he 'reigned c. 1500–1480 BC'); 'The state of Kizzuwatna in the west also shifted its allegiance to Mitanni'; 'The states of Aleppo in the west, and Nuzi and Arrapha in the east'. Cliopatria's first shape…
1445: Mitanni meets Thutmose III at Aleppo.
1438 (bridged): the fighting over the Aleppo region ends with Thutmose III's last Syrian campaign.

c. 1350 BC: Ashur-uballit I annexes Mitanni territory. The page dates him '(1365–1330 BC)' and has him annex it 'in the middle of the 14th century BC'; it names no cities, so the region is the part of the 1400 shape that neither the 1300 rump nor the Hittite share holds.

c. 1330 BC: Mitanni becomes the rump state of Hanigalbat. 'The middle part continued on as the rump state of Hanigalbat'; Shattiwaza, installed by a Hittite army 'in the late 14th century BC' and reigning 'c. 1330–1305 BC', ruled it as a Hittite dependent. The year is the reign's start, bridged; the page does not date…

c. 1330: Shattiwaza rules Mitanni as a Hittite vassal. A Hittite army 'installed Shattiwaza, the son of Tushratta, as their vassal king of Mitanni' 'in the late 14th century BC' and he 'reigned c. 1330–1305 BC' (Mitanni page, reopened 2026-10-19). Mitanni is the vassal and the Hittites the suzerain; this mirrors…

c. 1305 (bridged): the Hittite suzerainty over the rump ends with Shattiwaza's reign. The page ends his reign c. 1305 and has Adad-nirari I capture Shattuara (reign 'c. 1305–1285 BC'), with no year for the change of suzerain; mirrors hittites /ledger/10. Between this year and the Assyrian vassalage at -1300 the rump…

c. 1300: Hanigalbat becomes an Assyrian vassal. 'Adad-nirari claims to have captured King Shattuara and brought him to Ashur, where he took an oath as a vassal'; 'he was allowed to return to Mitanni, where he paid Adad-nirari regular tribute' (Mitanni page, reopened 2026-10-19). The page gives Shattuara 'c. 1305–1285…

c. 1300 (bridged): the Assyrians take Washukanni with the Khabur cities. 'Wasashatta ... attempted to rebel' and the Assyrians 'took Washukanni, Amasakku, Kahat, Shuru, Nabula, Hurra and Shuduhu as well' (Mitanni page). The page puts this in Wasashatta's reign ('c. 1285-1265 BC') and Adad-nirari I's (to 1275), i.e.…

c. 1250 BC: Shalmaneser I annexes Hanigalbat. The page dates Shattuara II's rebellion 'around 1250 BC' and says Shalmaneser I 'annexed the kingdom' in the 13th century; 'Mitanni was reduced to the status of a province of the Middle Assyrian Empire between c. 1350 and 1260 BC'. The infobox ends Mitanni c. 1260 BC…

c. 1250 BC: Mitanni ends as an Assyrian province. The page's infobox says disestablished c. 1260 BC and its text puts Shattuara II's rebellion c. 1250; the date taken here is the later one so that the rump keeps its Cliopatria shape.

c. 1250: the Assyrian suzerainty ends in annexation. Shattuara II 'rebelled against Assyrian control with the help of the Hittites' around 1250 BC and 'Shalmaneser I annexed the kingdom' (Mitanni page); the same year as the loss and dissolve below.

wars.name: Egyptian campaigns against Mitanni (Thutmose III)
wars.outcome: The Egyptian army crossed the Euphrates at Carchemish; no land changed hands and Mitanni later made peace with Egypt under Thutmose IV and Amenhotep III.

wars.name: Mitanni's sack of Assur
wars.outcome: Shaushtatar 'sacked the Assyrian capital of Assur'; no territorial change is recorded.

wars.name: Great Syrian War (Suppiluliuma I against Mitanni)
wars.outcome: Hittite victory: Washukanni sacked in 1345, Carchemish taken 1327, Shattiwaza installed as a dependent king of the rump.

wars.name: Assyrian conquest of Mitanni (Ashur-uballit I to Shalmaneser I)
wars.outcome: Ashur-uballit I annexes territory in the middle of the 14th century; Adad-nirari I takes Shattuara and later Washukanni; Shalmaneser I puts down Shattuara II's rebellion c.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line survives; the kingdom's extent is read from the lands that paid allegiance, so every edge is approximate.
